periods.analysis: Harborview 2030 opens this reporting series at 13% complete, status green, with no prior-quarter movement to calculate yet. The foundation is solid: the Community visioning survey is complete, the Land-use element is adopted, and the Housing & mobility element is now the active workstream with its draft due in 30 days. Planning staff and MIG’s neighborhood team closed the loop on survey coding for the Bayside, Hillcrest, and Marina District cohorts, which gives us a clean evidence trail for Council and keeps departments looking prepared. Council adoption of the full plan remains not-started and 150 days out, which is appropriate at this stage.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green status by locking the Housing & mobility draft review calendar now: Planning, Public Works, and Economic Development should each return one consolidated markup within 10 business days. Extend the data-quality practice by attaching the final survey crosstabs, land-use ordinance reference, and outreach map to the ClearPoint evidence tab before the next reporting cycle. Begin a light-touch Council adoption checklist so the 150-day milestone does not become a scramble later.

periods.analysis: Progress moved from 13% to 19%, a quarter-over-quarter gain of 6 percentage points, and the initiative remains green. That is the right pace for a comprehensive plan: not flashy, but disciplined, with the completed survey and adopted Land-use element continuing to anchor the story. The Housing & mobility element draft stayed in progress, and the team used Route 7 transit stop audits, ADU permit trends, and school-walkshed data to tighten the policy tables. Council adoption remains not-started and 150 days out, so we are still in the staff-and-stakeholder production window rather than the formal decision window.
periods.recommendations: Sustain momentum by publishing a two-page “what changed from survey to policy” memo for department directors before the January check-in. Extend the green performance by assigning named owners for each Housing & mobility subsection—housing supply, anti-displacement, bike/ped safety, and transit access—so draft comments come back cleanly. Keep the Council adoption item in preview mode only, but add tentative study-session dates to the master schedule.

periods.analysis: Harborview 2030 advanced from 19% to 25%, another 6-point quarter-over-quarter increase, with status still green. The pattern is exactly what we want for an AA-rated, fast-growing city: steady completion, traceable inputs, and no last-minute heroics. The Housing & mobility draft remained in progress, with staff reconciling coastal access comments from the North Pier workshop against the adopted Land-use element. Council adoption remains not-started and 150 days out, and that is acceptable because the policy draft still needs interdepartmental calibration before it becomes a Council product.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the reporting rhythm by holding the March draft reconciliation meeting with Planning, Public Works, Parks, and the City Attorney in one room rather than by email. Extend the evidence base by adding the North Pier workshop attendance log, translation counts, and comment disposition matrix to ClearPoint. Prepare a Council-facing milestone graphic now so elected officials can see the path from 25% complete to adoption without asking staff to rebuild the narrative later.

periods.analysis: The initiative moved from 25% to 31%, a 6-point quarter-over-quarter gain, and remains green. We are now past the early framework phase and into the careful alignment work that makes the final plan usable by departments after adoption. The Housing & mobility element draft stayed in progress while the team tested policy language against Harborview’s active permit pipeline on Harbor Boulevard, Seacliff Avenue, and the East Marina infill area. The Community visioning survey and Land-use element continue to be complete, and Council adoption remains not-started and 150 days out by design.
periods.recommendations: Sustain green performance by completing a policy-to-implementation crosswalk that names the lead department, likely funding source, and first-year action for each major Housing & mobility recommendation. Extend the operational usefulness of the plan by asking Development Services to review the draft against real permit types, including mixed-use, townhome, ADU, and frontage-improvement applications. Keep the adoption milestone protected by drafting the Council staff report shell now, even while substantive content is still maturing.

periods.analysis: Harborview 2030 increased from 31% to 37%, maintaining the same 6-point quarter-over-quarter movement and a green status. The work is maturing from drafting into validation, which is where Jamie’s favorite things matter: clean version control, clear owners, and no mystery numbers in the Council packet. The Housing & mobility element draft remains in progress, with consultant review focused on growth assumptions for the 14th Street corridor, ferry terminal access, and neighborhood-serving retail near Harborview High. Council adoption remains not-started and 150 days out, but the runway is visibly shorter now, so schedule discipline matters more each month.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green trajectory by freezing the baseline data tables for population, jobs, housing capacity, and commute mode share by the end of the quarter. Extend stakeholder confidence by hosting one targeted validation session with neighborhood associations and one with major employers before the draft is packaged for broader release. Add a ClearPoint note identifying which figures are final versus provisional so departments are not briefing from different versions.

periods.analysis: Progress moved from 37% to 43%, another 6-point quarter-over-quarter gain, and the initiative remains green. This is a healthy close to the calendar year: the completed visioning survey and adopted Land-use element are stable, while Housing & mobility remains in progress with enough detail to support real tradeoff conversations. Staff completed a winter accessibility scan along the Waterfront Loop, Old Mill Road, and the civic campus sidewalks to make sure the mobility recommendations are not just map-pretty but field-true. Council adoption remains not-started and 150 days out, which means our job is still to reduce ambiguity before the formal adoption path begins.
periods.recommendations: Sustain performance by issuing a year-end internal status memo that confirms the 43% complete figure, milestone states, and remaining decision points. Extend the quality-control practice by having GIS, Finance, and Public Works sign off on maps, cost bands, and capital-project references before any public draft is circulated. Use the next department head meeting to identify the top five policy issues likely to draw Council questions and assign one accountable responder for each.

periods.analysis: Harborview 2030 advanced from 18% to 23%, a 5-point quarter-over-quarter climb, and stays green. With the Land-use element adopted in March, the work has shifted from collecting good input to shaping a Council-ready, implementation-minded plan. The Housing & mobility draft remains in progress, with the team tightening language on missing-middle housing, coastal evacuation routes, and frequent-transit access so it fits both neighborhood expectations and operational reality. Council adoption remains not-started and roughly nine months out, but the adoption sequence is close enough that we should treat every edit as if it may appear in the final packet.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green status by running a pre-adoption readiness review with the City Manager’s Office, City Attorney, and Communications before the next public release. Extend the plan’s credibility by adding a one-page implementation dashboard prototype showing first-year actions, responsible departments, and likely reporting measures. Keep the 23% figure well-supported by uploading the draft chapter index, comment log, and readiness-review agenda to ClearPoint.

periods.analysis: The initiative moved from 23% to 43%, a 20-point quarter-over-quarter gain — the largest of the plan so far — and remains green. Approaching the midpoint is meaningful: Harborview 2030 now has completed visioning, an adopted Land-use element, and a substantially developed Housing & mobility draft still in progress. Staff and the consultant team used the spring permit surge—especially along Seacliff Avenue and the East Marina infill nodes—to stress-test whether the draft policies will work for a city of 165,000 that is still growing quickly. Council adoption remains not-started and about six months out, so we are on schedule, but the next arc needs to move from draft refinement to adoption readiness.
periods.recommendations: Sustain momentum by setting a firm 30-day closeout plan for the Housing & mobility element draft, with weekly Friday owner check-ins and one final executive review. Extend the green result by preparing the Council adoption workplan now: study session, public hearing, Planning Commission recommendation, final Council packet, and communications timeline. Maintain data quality by reconciling all plan metrics to the City Strategic Plan scorecard before the next quarterly report, so the 43% complete status is easy for Council to trust.

periods.analysis: 70% complete. 0 of 4 milestones are done. Next up: Community visioning survey complete (due Sep 29, 2025).
periods.recommendations: Review the late milestones with the project owner and confirm recovery dates before the next reporting cycle.
